question: Which steering methods can move a DIFFUSE feature without breaking the model? Neuron-level edits failed today (clusters rarely beat single neurons; natural-range surgery null; pairs collapse); the census says shared structure is a few residual directions seen through a smearing neuron basis. Compare the ladder: neuron cluster -> mean-difference direction -> the diffuse set's combined write -> a tiny trained intervention, at matched push strength, on harmless features.
model: Qwen/Qwen3-4B bf16, chat template, enable_thinking=False, greedy.

formality: Respond in a very formal, polished register.
Respond in a very casual, chatty register.
sadness: Respond in a sad, melancholic tone.
food: Work food and cooking into your answer.

data: 40 training prompts (everyday questions); the model writes a 60-token reply under the positive and the contrast instruction. 20 HELD-OUT prompts for evaluation, never used to build any method. Replies are then teacher-forced after the PLAIN prompt (no instruction) to read activations.

methods.A_neurons: the 64 neurons on floors 12-20 with the largest |t| of (positive - contrast) mean activation over reply tokens; each pushed additively at its own floor by its signed t, the summed residual push scaled to the matched norm.
methods.B_direction: mean over reply tokens of the residual at floor 16, positive minus contrast, averaged over pairs; added at floor 16, all positions.
methods.C_diffuse_write: the top-200 neurons (floors 12-20) by |t|: v = sum t_n * W_down[:,n]; added at floor 16 (the whole diffuse population as one push).
methods.D_trained: rank-4 residual adapter at floor 16, h' = h + A(Bh + c), trained (Adam, 150 steps, frozen model) to maximise the likelihood of the POSITIVE replies after the PLAIN prompts. Evaluated at scale 0.5/1/1.5/2 of its learned edit; its x-position is its measured mean ||delta|| / ||h||.

strength: x = push norm / mean residual norm at floor 16 on the held-out prompts; A/B/C at x in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.8}.
metrics: on 20 held-out prompts, 60 tokens: EFFECT = mean self-judge score (unsteered model: 'Is this reply <formal|sad|about food>? Answer Yes or No.', logit Yes - No) minus the unsteered baseline; BREAKING = mean per-token NLL of the steered reply under the unsteered model (minus baseline) and rep4; CAPABILITY = 16 factual QA (answer-key match, reframe-gate-vireo set).
H1: B (direction) reaches a larger effect than A (neuron cluster) at every NLL increase up to +1.0 nat/token.
H2: C (diffuse write) behaves like B, not like A (aggregate steering of the diffuse set works where per-neuron did not).
H3: D (trained, rank 4) gets the largest effect at <= +0.5 nat/token NLL and keeps capability >= 14/16, for >= 2 of 3 features.
